title: Building a General LangGraph MCP Server for Assistants and Threads
summary: Riccardo Pirruccio builds a general-purpose LangGraph MCP server that lists, inspects and runs assistants and reads thread state.
learn: LangGraph is LangChain's abstraction for creating agent systems, with a lot of control over how they are built and how state is managed.
Because LangGraph graphs can now be exposed as an API, the MCP can be general instead of tailored to a single graph.
An assistant is an instance of a graph with certain configurations embedded, such as the model or an API key, and one graph can have many assistants.
A thread preserves state, so a thread can be reused however many times is needed, while a stateless run keeps none.
The first three tools list assistants through the LangGraph Python SDK search API, fetch an assistant's schema, and run an assistant with the input that schema describes.

Running an assistant timed out with the slow-thinking R1 model, so Pirruccio added tools to search threads and read thread state, then demos the MCP against a graph running in Docker, switching from Claude Desktop to Cline when Claude fails.
